title: Double Caching (Application Memory Cache over DB Memory Buffer)
pattern: Caching retrieved database rows inside an in-memory application dictionary to "avoid database lookup overhead."
why_bad: Modern databases (like SQLite, Postgres, or MongoDB) already maintain highly optimized, size-bounded buffer caches in RAM. Application-level caching causes double RAM consumption, stale data sync bugs, and wastes CPU cycles on serialization [82, 128].
detection: A dictionary cache containing raw database row structures that are queried inside application services where the DB is local or already fully buffered.
counterexample: A distributed cache cluster (like Memcached or Redis) separating slow remote disks from fast serving clusters. `Context-dependent`.
fix: Query the database directly on-demand and configure the database buffer pool size correctly.
